newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKR group wins Tokyo development project.
newsitem.headline: HKR group wins Tokyo development project.

text.p: A consortium including HKR International Ltd has won a contract to develop a commercial complex in central Tokyo, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.
The consortium acquired a 211,670 square foot plot in Minato ward for HK$8.82 billion and plans to build a commercial complex including office and retail space, it said.
The consortium includes companies from Japan, Hong Kong and Singapore, and the plot is part of a site owned by the Japanese National Railway Settlement Corp.

HKR said development costs were estimated to be HK$20 billion. Its attributable interest in the project may range from 4.5 to 10 percent, bringing its financial commitments to between HK$900 million and HK$2.0 billion, HKR said.
Planning and construction were expected to take about six to seven years.

"The investment in the consortium represents an attractive opportunity to participate in the Tokyo real estate market at an acceptable price and on a shared basis and is in line with the policy of HKRI to extend its investment base beyond Hong Kong and into the leading real estate markets of the region," the companyy said.
HKR said it intends to hold the completed property as a long-term investment and that its investment would be financed by internal funding and external financing.
About 60 percent of the funding commitment would be obtained from financial institutions, it said.
Mingly Corp owns about 57.32 percent of HKR International.
